equivalents.proof: peek() has already established length <= available. Each iteration copies min(remaining chunk bytes, requested bytes still unwritten), so written cannot exceed length. Once written equals length, any remaining valid queue entries contribute a zero-length subarray and a zero-length set at offset length. The changed OR only visits these extra zero-copy entries; it exits at queue length and does not change state or output. Re-reviewed after introducing the head cursor: the loop begins at headIndex; only indices below headIndex are cleared, so every visited entry remains defined. available equals the sum of active entries from headIndex onward, less headOffset. Prefix compaction preserves their order and these invariants. The original reasoning therefore continues to apply to the active suffix.

equivalents.proof: Both streaming and bounded-probe paths call decodeTagHeader before using hasFooter. It rejects versions outside 2..4 and flags outside 0xc0 for v2.2 or 0xe0 for v2.3; those masks exclude footer bit0x10. Only v2.4 can therefore reach hasFooter with that bit set. Replacing this final version test with true changes neither the header result, streaming skip/footer checks nor probe boundary evidence. equivalents.proof: The private decoder has two strict callers, readTagHeader and probeTagEnvelope, which prove a complete ten-byte header before calling. Its only incomplete-input caller is hasPossibleMetadataPrefix, which observes metadata plausibility, not the returned header or size. For a still-plausible prefix shorter than ten bytes, every available size byte has already passed the synchsafe check. Missing size bytes coerce to zero in the bounded bitwise size expression, so bodyLength remains nonnegative. A computed footer begins at least ten bytes from the prefix start, beyond all available bytes; its supplied footer view is empty and matchesFooterPrefix returns true. Without a footer the other branch likewise returns true. The original undefined result also returns true immediately. Invalid prefixes still throw at the same earlier validation and become false in the same caller. No reader method, iterator operation, cursor, propagated error, returned count or resource ownership changes. Only a fixed local header object and bounded arithmetic are added; neither retained-input size nor asymptotic memory/work bounds change.

equivalents.assumptions: Ordinary immutable Buffer/Uint8Array input produced by inferFreeFormatBaseLength at a recognized free-format header; first is decoded from the same window at offset zero. No proxies, overridden typed-array methods, concurrent mutation or detachment, private-state reflection or prototype monkey-patching. The observable contract includes returned counts, typed errors, evidence selection, accounted work and explicit cooperative-yield/cancellation checkpoints, not identical instruction counts or nanosecond CPU/GC timing. Bounded local operations must preserve upload-length-independent memory and work bounds.
equivalents.proof: indexOffset(0) must add the recognized initial free header, making the mutated landmarks [sentinel, 0, ...ascending numeric landmarks]. Every landmarkStart call receives a minimum >= 20, including suffix calls. The ordinary numeric zero is strictly below the sought minimum. In the lower-bound binary search, any midpoint at index >= 1 has exactly the original numeric predicate. Its insertion point is therefore >= 2; it cannot finish at or before index 1 because that element is < minimum. The nonnumeric sentinel at index 0 is never selected or used in candidate arithmetic. All original eligible numeric landmarks are enumerated in the same order with the same values; only array indices shift by one. Consequently followCandidate, side/metadata observations, caches, work totals, yielded values, and selection/error paths are identical. The sentinel never reaches subtraction or any native parser error path. The extra constant array slot and possibly a different bounded binary-search comparison path do not change the upload-length-independent memory/work bound. No work-reserve or yield call is added. This proof depends on the real initial header at offset 0; an arbitrary isolated new Probe(empty, ...) or dishonest analyzer first is outside this production-call domain.

equivalents.proof: any is called only from shortIsUnambiguous after each candidate frame meets its mandatory prefix. stop = min(through + 1, window.length) is a valid nonnegative prefix index. Each unmutated prefix array starts at zero and adds only 0 or 1 per indexed byte. Since at most 8,647 bytes are indexed, no Uint16 overflow occurs: each array is nondecreasing on valid indices. When from < stop, evaluation is unchanged. When from === stop, strict comparison reads the same value twice and is false. When from > stop and in range, monotonicity gives prefix[stop] <= prefix[from], also false. When from lies beyond the array, the right operand is undefined, whose numeric comparison is false. Candidate starts ensure from is never negative in the original source. Thus the added comparisons return false on exactly the previously short-circuited cases. They have no side effects, cannot throw, and add no cache/work/yield operations. shortIsUnambiguous and every downstream accepted count/error remain identical. Prefix monotonicity and the 8,647-byte bound are essential assumptions; unrestricted larger helper inputs that wrap Uint16 are not covered.

equivalents.proof: Exact change: probe.suffixes.get(offset)?.credible becomes probe.suffixes.get(offset).credible in isSupportedTransition. In the scoped parser, first is decoded from the valid free header at window offset zero. Probe.headers inserts exactly the valid indexed/free headers in increasing window-offset order. Every call to isSupportedTransition is made by followCandidate only after end = position + base + padding with base >= 20 and padding >= 0, and after a successful metadata observation whose returned offset is at least end. Thus queried offset is strictly greater than the candidate start and is never zero. If next is undefined, or its rate equals the current candidate rate, evaluation short-circuits before either property access. Otherwise: (a) while evaluating a suffix, the reverse dynamic program has already stored SuffixEvidence for every greater-offset valid header; (b) while evaluating the root, any header with a rate different from root first necessarily made entries.some(...) true, so the completed reverse loop populated every non-root header. When that loop did not run, every stored header has the root first rate and the differing-rate conjunct is false. Therefore whenever either access is reached, the key exists and its value is a non-undefined SuffixEvidence object. Both expressions return the identical credible boolean; neither adds/removes work reservations, yields, side effects, errors or reader operations. This proof assumes production-consistent first/window input and the unmodified increasing-offset Probe and metadata semantics; it is not a claim about callers fabricating an inconsistent internal helper argument or mutating private probe maps.
